candidates.exact_span: Select only those Elements and Sections which apply to your sludge reuse or disposal practice.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which Elements and Sections apply determines which numeric limits are in scope (A), which monitoring and reporting obligations attach (B), and what evidence is expected versus legitimately absent (C).

candidates.exact_span: If your facility utilizes more than one type of disposal or reuse method (for example, Element I and Element II apply) or the quality of your sludge varies (for example, Section II and Section III of Element I apply) use a separate Discharge Monitoring Report (DMR) for each Section that is applicable.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether multiple disposal methods or sludge-quality categories are in use changes how many DMRs must be filed and which section-specific monitoring evidence is required; misinterpreting this could misclassify missing reports as non-required or vice versa.

candidates.exact_span: The sludge DMRs shall be due by February 19th of each year and shall cover the previous January through December time period. (The sludge DMRs for permits in Texas shall be due by September 1 of each year, with the reporting period of August 1 to July 31)
candidates.computation_change_reason: The applicable due date and reporting-period boundaries (calendar year vs Texas August–July) determine which monitoring periods fall within Federal FY2025, which reported measurements are in scope for limit comparison, and whether absent reports represent missing evidence or fall outside the evaluated period.

candidates.exact_span: The sludge conditions do not apply to wastewater treatment lagoons where sludge is not wasted for final reuse/disposal.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a lagoon facility wastes sludge for final reuse/disposal determines if sludge conditions—and their associated limits, monitoring, and reporting—apply at all.

candidates.exact_span: If the sludge is not removed, the permittee shall indicate on the DMR "No Discharge".
candidates.computation_change_reason: This establishes a specific documented no-discharge reporting obligation and the form of evidence (DMR notation) that distinguishes a permitted no-data state from inadequate evidence of required monitoring.

candidates.exact_span: Requirements Specific to Bulk Sewage Sludge for Application to the Land Meeting Class A or B Pathogen Reduction and the Cumulative Loading Rates in Table 2, or Class B Pathogen Reduction and the Pollutant Concentrations in Table 3
candidates.computation_change_reason: Pathogen class (A vs B) and whether compliance is measured against Table 2 cumulative loading rates or Table 3 pollutant concentrations select different enforceable numeric limits and section-specific monitoring requirements.

candidates.exact_span: Requirements Specific to Bulk Sewage Sludge Meeting Pollutant Concentrations in Table 3 and Class A Pathogen Reduction Requirements
candidates.computation_change_reason: Applicability of Section III hinges on meeting Table 3 pollutant concentrations and Class A pathogen reduction; different interpretations of those thresholds change which limits and monitoring obligations govern.

candidates.exact_span: Requirements Specific to Sludge Sold or Given Away in a Bag or Other Container for Application to the Land that does not meet the Pollutant Concentrations in Table 3
candidates.computation_change_reason: Section IV applies only when packaged sludge fails Table 3 pollutant concentrations; whether that condition is met routes the facility to a different requirement set with distinct limits and monitoring.

candidates.exact_span: Requirements Specific to Surface Disposal Sites Without a Liner and Leachate Collection System
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a surface disposal site lacks a liner and leachate collection system determines applicability of Element 2 Section II versus Section III, which carry different requirement sets.

candidates.exact_span: Requirements Specific to Surface Disposal Sites With a Liner and Leachate Collection System
candidates.computation_change_reason: Presence of a liner and leachate collection system selects Section III over Section II for surface disposal, changing which numeric limits and monitoring conditions apply.
